title: LIN-4349 P4: autopilot precedence written once; landed under real work; the scoped-run tail
description:
## As asked

## This piece: P4 of 4 (after P3)

Autopilot's order is written once, with `landed` ranked under real work, and a scoped run takes one Periodical as it finishes (John's ruling, 8 Nov: "Yes, add the scoped-run tail in piece 4").

### Files and approach (from the approved plan)

* **New import-free leaf** `lib/prompts/autopilot-precedence.js`, exporting `AUTOPILOT_PRECEDENCE`. `lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js` renders it once, in place of both conflicting orders (Orient at about line 485, first act at about lines 720–735).
  * General order:
    1. a goal from the human;
    2. a weekly-floor `due` lane;
    3. movable stack work;
    4. a `landed` lane, oldest last run first, one at a time, only when no stack work can move now.
  * "No stack work can move now" means every remaining task is in Backlog, waiting on a person, blocked or already running.
  * **Builder note 2:** a repo-scoped lane reading `never` is treated as the most overdue `due`, including in the tail. Otherwise evidence older than the 30-day horizon drops the lane out of every rank. No fold change is needed.
  * **The scoped-run tail:**
    * After its own task is merged and verified, a scoped run reads `GET /periodicals`, takes at most one eligible repo-scoped lane, drives its review and stops.
    * Floor work (`due`, including `never`) goes before `landed`, then the oldest last run.
    * Recent Headwinds (workspace-scoped) stays with general runs.
    * **Builder note 3:** read after verification, not in the same beat as the Done write, because merge recording is asynchronous.
  * Ranks 2 and 4 and the tail dispatch through the existing `POST /periodicals/{id}/mint`, with `repo` for named lanes, keeping the opening `periodicalId` stamp.
* **Docs:**
  * Replace the live precedence restatements with pointers to the constant in:
    * `docs/autopilot.md` §6 (every restatement, about lines 170–191, 360 and 368);
    * `docs/autopilot-kickoff.md` (the maintainer note);
    * `docs/architecture/source-map.md`;
    * `docs/plans/survey.md` ("has no such rank today").
  * Mark `docs/autopilot-orchestrator-prompt.md`'s Stage B order (about lines 66–70) as historical, with a pointer.
  * Leave dated session logs (e.g. `docs/collective-session-2026-06-12.md`) as written.
  * Search: `grep -rn "periodical reading\|overdue periodical\|past its cadence threshold\|precedence" lib docs`.
* Do not turn precedence into a computed decision engine.

### Acceptance and witnesses

* The LIN-1829 scoped snapshot test is updated on purpose. A new assertion pins that the periodicals read happens only after task completion, and that `never` is handled alongside `due`.
* An anti-duplication test, following `tests/unit/lin-4374-review-leftover-read.test.js`, fails when:
  * any `lib/` or `routes/` file other than the leaf spells out the ranks;
  * the docs fail to name `AUTOPILOT_PRECEDENCE`.
* If a kickoff ceiling exists in `tests/unit/prompt-size-budget.test.js` after rebase, re-measure it and explain the change. There is none at `110e35e0`.
* **Spend ceiling, as approved:** at most one Periodical (two sessions) per finished scoped task, and up to 15 lanes × 2 sessions per idle day, with one-day landed spacing.

### After this lands (parent's Done witness, recorded on LIN-4349, not built here)

* A merge produces `landed` in `GET /periodicals`.
* An automatic review merges its guarded notes/report PR with no follow-up tickets.
* The next scoping or build in that area cites the entry.
* One immediate miss right after a merge is not a failure, because recording is asynchronous.

**Parent:** LIN-4349, "The Periodicals run when work lands, and feed the look-first step". Read the parent's description in full: the `## As asked` block (the person's words, unchanged), and the `## Implementation Plan` (rev 2). The approving plan review is comment `b79ff49e-c3db-46e1-8071-8d9c89402097` on LIN-4349; its "Notes for the builder" are part of this piece where they name it.

**Starting point:** the parent's approved plan is where this piece starts. Follow it. Where the code shows it is wrong, change course at the cause and say so on LIN-4349.

**Grounding commit:** `110e35e053ec6ef181f4e230111c6b7f0ade7d9f` (main, 2026-11-08). Main had not moved when this was split (checked 2026-11-08 10:1x UTC). Re-check `git log 110e35e0..main` for the paths below before building.

Session fit: fits one session

Plan-review due: no — covered by LIN-4349's approving plan-review (comment b79ff49e-c3db-46e1-8071-8d9c89402097, rev 2)

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Size of the move

**Size:** just the task
**Why:** Writes autopilot's order once, landed work ranked below movable stack work, and gives a finished scoped run one Periodical; rewriting the scoped run's old promises and stopping chained tails belong to it, since the ask fails without them.
**Cuts:** none
**Decided by:** the standing policy

## Outcome

Implemented and merged in PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2379](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2379>). The merge commit is `a478e5d9`, deployed 8 Nov 16:16 UTC. `AUTOPILOT_PRECEDENCE` in `lib/prompts/autopilot-precedence.js` is the one spelling of autopilot's order. It is rendered once in the kickoff's Orient, with `landed` at rank 4 under movable stack work. A finished scoped run takes the tail: at most one repo-scoped Periodical, minted with `autopilot: true`, then the run stops. A Periodical's own review task takes no tail.

The plan was implemented as approved, with two departures recorded on LIN-4349 (comment `70a5af4c`): the tail mints and stops instead of driving the review inline, and `GET /periodicals` exposes `scope`. The live behavioural witnesses (tail, chain guard, spend) are recorded as not yet run on LIN-4349 (comment `5979a0f5`). The full stage history is preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

comments.body:
## Survey open-0: LIN-4382 @ 3272fe4a6

**The grounding commit is stale.** `110e35e0` is 84 commits behind, and P3 (LIN-4381, #2376) has landed since. P3 already edited the first act (`lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js:720-726`), and it added interim wording that this piece has to remove: *"`landed` … rank it as `recent`"*. There's still no kickoff ceiling in `prompt-size-budget.test.js`.

### Why this will be hard

1. **The tail goes against what a scoped run is told it is.** The scoped goal block (`:705-710`) says "the precedence policy is moot" and "Do not pull other tasks off the stack", and a test pins that. The finish line has to become "verified, then one read, one lane, stop", without the run taking it as permission to keep walking the stack.

2. **"Drives its review" is ambiguous, and the server may refuse it.** `POST /periodicals/{id}/mint` stamps `periodicalId` on the mint row (`lib/dispatch-entrance.js:2035`), and its `autopilot: true` variant hands Stage 2 to a separate kickoff. If the scoped run drives the review issue itself through `recommend-and-dispatch`, that's a second distinct task. `guardBudget` (`lib/dispatch-factory.js:391-410`) then refuses it with `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` on any run declaring `maxTasks: 1`. The approved spend ceiling ("one Periodical (two sessions)") reads like the mint-plus-handoff version.

3. **Stamping.** Today rank 2 stamps `periodicalId` on the chain-opening `recommend-and-dispatch` (`:730-736`), while the plan sends ranks 2 and 4 and the tail through mint. P3's self-trigger exclusion (`_periodicalIssues`, `lib/periodical-runs.js:218-243`) depends on those writers, as its comment warns. If a Periodical's own merge goes unexcluded, every lane reads `landed` again. `lin-4381-landed-route.test.js` must stay green.

4. **The tests pin two orders deliberately.** All of these are in `tests/unit/autopilot-kickoff.test.js`:
   - the scoped golden fixture, which is built to catch exactly this edit;
   - "periodicals pointer never appears in scoped output" (`:516`), which must be inverted, not dropped;
   - the "three-level precedence" string test;
   - the "supersedes the Orient step's two-level order" test;
   - "guide's two-level Orient list still renders verbatim, unconditionally".

   Writing the order once makes every one of them wrong, on purpose.

5. **The anti-duplication pattern.** "Spells out the ranks" needs a pattern that catches a paraphrase but not ordinary use: `precedence` already appears in about 30 unrelated `lib/` files.

### Deeper than the ticket

The real defect is two orders: the guide's Orient and the snapshot's first act, with a "supersedes" patch between them. Each piece since LIN-1829 has patched one and pinned the other. Keep the leaf to one rendered block plus one tail paragraph, with no general/scoped/stepper branching inside it. That's the cheapest way to keep "no decision engine".

### What I'd do first

Before editing, decide whether the tail mints with `autopilot: true` and stops, or drives Stage 2 itself. I recommend minting: it avoids the budget clash, mint brings its own stamp, and it fits the two-session ceiling. Record the decision on LIN-4349, since it changes the plan's "drives its review". Then write the leaf, delete the Orient order and the supersedes clause together, and rewrite those tests in the same commit.

## Survey global: LIN-4382 @ 3bfa70b29

Main is 85 commits past `110e35e0`. P3 (LIN-4381) is in and adds an interim "rank `landed` as `recent` until LIN-4382". There is still no kickoff ceiling.

**Where it lands.** `lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js` is 763 lines of template literals in one function, edited 22 times since September. Two orders are live in it: Orient's two-level list (l.485), which renders in **both** modes, and the general first act's "supersedes" clause (l.720–736). The docs restate the order about six times in three wordings. `docs/autopilot-kickoff.md` is a hand mirror ("must not drift"), and no test checks it. Things are improving: one spelling per leaf (`leftover-words.js`, `area-registry-path.js`) is the current habit, and this task follows it.

**What the obvious build does.**
- **The scoped half undoes LIN-1829's rule on purpose, and it touches more text than the ticket names.** Scoped output was kept unchanged *by construction*: the golden fixture, "periodicals pointer never appears in scoped output" (test l.516), and the maintainer note. The scoped goal block ("precedence policy is moot … Do not pull other tasks off the stack") and the file header (l.11–16) also have to change. If only the first act changes, the scoped prompt contradicts itself.
- **The tail can chain.** Mint + Autopilot (`periodicals.js` l.1189) starts a *scoped* autopilot on the review task it mints. When that run finishes, the tail takes the next `due`/`never` lane, and so on until the floor is clear. LIN-4381's self-trigger exclusion covers `landed` only. Each run keeps "one per finished scoped task", but the chain does not. The tail needs a rule that it skips a Periodical's own review task (gate marker, `resolvePeriodicalIdFromGateMarker`), and a test for it. Callers pass different `issue` shapes (`workspace-api-prompts.js` passes only `{identifier, title}`), so a code-side check would not see the same data on every path.
- **Two ways to dispatch.** The first act today stamps `periodicalId` on `recommend-and-dispatch`, and the kickoff never mentions `/mint`. If ranks 2 and 4 move to mint, the old paragraph must go, or both stay live. Also check that minting and then driving the minted task fits a scoped run's `maxTasks`.
- **The anti-duplication test needs rank phrases, not the word "precedence".** That word matches about 40 unrelated lines in `lib/`. The existing "walk the stack under the precedence policy" lines are pointers and can stay.

**Better, at this task's cost.** Render the leaf once, in Orient. Delete the supersedes clause and the interim line. Rewrite the scoped goal block from "moot" to "your task, then the tail". Put the tail's order in the same leaf so it isn't a second copy. Make the maintainer note a pointer. Update the golden test once, with the reason.

**Better still, not this task's.** The unchecked doc mirror. Splitting the kickoff into named sections, so that "scoped untouched" holds by structure rather than by a golden file. A periodical-origin flag that every kickoff caller passes the same way.

**LIN-4382 implementation: PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2379.** Commit `236001232`, branched from main `3bfa70b29`. CI is green: all 7 checks pass, including `CI success` (run 42495844125). Not merged; that waits for review.

**What it does**
- **`AUTOPILOT_PRECEDENCE`** (`lib/prompts/autopilot-precedence.js`, imports nothing) is now the one spelling of the order: a human goal, then `due` (the weekly floor), then the stack, then `landed` only when no stack work can move now, oldest first, one in flight. A repo-scoped `never` counts as the most overdue `due`.
- **The kickoff renders it once, in Orient, for every mode.** The "supersedes" first-act order and P3's interim "rank `landed` as `recent`" line are deleted.
- **The tail.** Once its own task is merged and verified, a scoped run reads `GET /periodicals`, mints one repo-scoped lane (`due`/`never` first) with `autopilot: true`, and stops. The scoped goal block, step 5, the file header and the operating manual now say "your task, then the tail". The old "moot" wording is gone.
- **Chain guard.** `POST /autopilot/kickoff` resolves the gate marker and tells a run on a Periodical's review task that it takes no tail. The policy's marker rule covers every other caller.
- **`GET /periodicals` publishes `scope`.** It is additive, and the repo-only rules need it.
- **Docs** point at the constant instead of restating the order. The Stage B order is marked historical.

**Witnesses**
- `tests/unit/lin-4382-precedence-written-once.test.js` (18 tests):
  - fails when `lib/` or `routes/` restates the ranks, or a doc stops naming the constant;
  - checks one rendering in each of the three modes;
  - checks marker parity;
  - includes a route-level kickoff guard test.

  Against main's kickoff and entrance code it fails in 12 places. Output is recorded in the PR.
- The LIN-1829 scoped golden was re-captured on purpose, and its only diff is the goal block. The "never in scoped output" test is inverted: the read now appears only after merged-and-verified, and `never` is handled beside `due`.
- No kickoff ceiling exists in `prompt-size-budget.test.js`, so nothing was re-measured.

**Departures from the plan** are recorded on LIN-4349 (comment `70a5af4c`): mint-and-stop instead of driving the review in the same run, and publishing `scope`. Neither cuts the `## As asked` block.

**Leftovers** (for the leftover step; both notes are near their byte cap):
- only `POST /autopilot/kickoff` passes `periodicalReview`; the UI and feedback kickoffs rely on the marker rule;
- `docs/autopilot-kickoff.md` is still an unchecked hand mirror.

### Leftovers

PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2379, head `ce92d171215169c2d275d1b5c49970aa0c231e86`. All 7 checks pass on it, including `CI success` (run 42496996734).

- **tidied:** `lib/periodical-runs.js`. The comment on the landed self-exclusion still said the opening `periodicalId` stamp lives in the kickoff; it now points at `AUTOPILOT_PRECEDENCE` in `lib/prompts/autopilot-precedence.js`.
- **noted (Lesson):** `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md`. Autopilot's order has one home, `lib/prompts/autopilot-precedence.js`: never restate a rank, because a census test fails on a copy. I distilled neighbouring wording to stay under the 6144-byte cap.
- **noted (Waiting):** `docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md`. Only `POST /autopilot/kickoff` passes `periodicalReview`. The UI and feedback kickoffs send `{identifier, title}` and rely on the policy's marker rule. I distilled wording here too to fit the cap.
- **for close-out:** nothing.

Not counted as leftovers:
- `docs/papers/harbour/steady-base-rules.json` still describes the old two-level order. It is a dated paper's evidence, so I left it as written, as with the session logs.
- `docs/autopilot-kickoff.md` is a hand mirror that no test checks. That gap predates this change (survey global, "Better still, not this task's").

## Review — LIN-4382

PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2379, head `ce92d171215169c2d275d1b5c49970aa0c231e86`. The head already contains main `393c7686b` (LIN-4393), and it merges cleanly.

CI: green on `ce92d171`. All 7 checks pass: Unit tests, E2E 1–4/4, Secret scan, CI success. I also re-ran locally on the head: 151/151 pass across `lin-4382-precedence-written-once`, `autopilot-kickoff`, `lin-4381-landed-route` and `proxy-periodicals-route`.

### Scope against what was asked and the plan
- **Leaf.** `lib/prompts/autopilot-precedence.js` imports nothing and exports `AUTOPILOT_PRECEDENCE`. It lists the four ranks in the order asked. "No stack work can move now" is spelled out as Backlog / waiting on a person / blocked / already running. The leaf also covers oldest-first with one in flight, and a repo-scoped `never` counting as the most overdue `due` (builder note 2). The tail reads after verification, not in the same beat as the Done write (builder note 3). It puts `due`/`never` before `landed`, then oldest. Workspace-scoped lanes (Recent Headwinds) are left to general runs. The leaf has no branching, so it is not a decision engine.
- **Rendered once.** The kickoff renders the leaf once, in Orient, for general, scoped and stepper runs. Removed together: the Orient two-level list, the first act's "supersedes" order, P3's interim "rank it as `recent`", and the scoped "precedence policy is moot". The scoped goal block, step 5 and the file header now say "your task, then the tail".
- **Docs.** `docs/autopilot.md`, `docs/autopilot-kickoff.md`, `source-map.md` and `survey.md` now point at the constant. The Stage B order in `autopilot-orchestrator-prompt.md` is marked historical, with a pointer. Session logs and `docs/papers/` are left as written. I re-ran the ticket's grep: no live restatement is left in `lib/`, `routes/` or `docs/`.
- **Changes beyond the plan.** There are two, both recorded on LIN-4349 (`70a5af4c`) as the block's own "change course at the cause and say so on LIN-4349" asks:
  1. The tail mints with `autopilot: true` and stops, instead of driving the review in the same run. I checked the cause: `guardBudget` (`lib/dispatch-factory.js:391`) refuses a second distinct task on a run declaring `maxTasks`. Mint's own `periodicalId` stamp and the gate-marker stamp keep P3's `_periodicalIssues` exclusion fed.
  2. `GET /periodicals` now returns `scope`. This is additive, and the repo-only rules can't be applied without it.

  The review still gets driven, by the run the tail launches. I read "drives its review" as met through that handoff, not narrowed. The spend effect is in the ledger.
- **Chain guard.** `POST /autopilot/kickoff` sets `periodicalReview` from `resolvePeriodicalIdFromGateMarker(found.issue.description)` (`lib/dispatch-entrance.js:1853`). Two things I checked:
  - Stage 1 is told to write the marker into the new task's description when it creates it (`lib/periodicals.js:246`), before the handoff kickoff.
  - The resolver finds the marker inside a sealed `## As asked` block. I tried it: `seams-tangles` resolves.

### Regression check
`git log` on the touched files (`autopilot-kickoff.js`, `dispatch-entrance.js`, `proxy-compute.js`, `periodical-runs.js`) shows no revert being re-applied. P3's three commits are intact: the store wiring, landed, and the lane-state wording. `lin-4381-landed-route` and the P3 wiring test stay green. The only change to P3 code is the stamp comment, which now points at the leaf, plus the additive `scope` field.

### Isolated, or one of a class?
The class is "an order restated outside its owner". The census in `lin-4382-precedence-written-once.test.js` sweeps every `.js` file in `lib/` and `routes/` for both the old and new rank phrasings. The docs test covers the four pointer docs. I found no unhandled sibling. `docs/papers/harbour/steady-base-rules.json` is dated evidence, rightly left as written.

### Tests and mutation checks
I made each change below, ran the tests, and reverted it. Every one went red:
- **M1.** `st.periodicalReview = null` in `dispatch-entrance.js`: the route-level kickoff guard test fails (1).
- **M2.** Appended "overdue periodical" to `lib/proxy-instructions.js`: the census fails (1).
- **M3.** Dropped `${precedence}` from the kickoff: 11 fail across the new test and `autopilot-kickoff`.
- **M4.** Dropped `scope: r.scope` in `routes/proxy-compute.js`: 2 fail.
- **M5.** Dropped `scope: template.scope` in the fold: 2 fail.
- **M6.** Removed the scoped goal block's tail sentence: 4 fail.

The test levels are right. The guard is witnessed through the real route against a seeded LocalProvider with a gate-marked task. The prompt text is pinned by unit tests. The scoped golden was re-captured on purpose, and its diff is only the goal block. "Never in scoped output" was inverted, not dropped: the read now has to come after "merged and verified". Nothing in CI can drive a model following the tail; that is in the ledger. `prompt-size-budget.test.js` has no kickoff ceiling, so nothing needed re-measuring.

Checklist: no security surface beyond an additive read field and a server-side marker read. Error handling is unchanged: a missing marker gives null, which leaves the output byte-identical. Style matches the codebase. No performance effect.

### Leftovers
The builder's `### Leftovers` matches the diff:
- **tidied:** the stamp comment in `lib/periodical-runs.js`.
- **noted (Lesson):** `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md`.
- **noted (Waiting):** `docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md`, for the `periodicalReview` caller gap.

I found no other edge. The unchecked `docs/autopilot-kickoff.md` mirror predates this change, and this PR keeps the mirror in sync (Orient pointer, step 5 tail). It is outside this change and listed below as outside.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside (the scoped-run tail).** A live scoped run follows the tail. This is model behaviour from prompt text, and no automated test drives it. **After the deploy**, on LIN-4349 as part of the parent's Done witness: let a scoped autopilot run's own task merge and verify while `GET /periodicals` shows a `scope: "repo"` lane reading `due`, `never` or `landed`. Right looks like this: after the Verified check, that run's session makes exactly one `POST /periodicals/{id}/mint` with `"autopilot": true` (`due`/`never` before `landed`), then stops. Wrong looks like: no mint, or a second mint, or a mint before the merge, or a `/recommend-and-dispatch` on any other task. One miss with `recent` showing right after the merge is not a failure, because recording is asynchronous (builder note 3).
- **Inside (chain guard, "prevent recursive tails").** The live Mint + Autopilot handoff carries the no-tail line. CI seeds the marker itself. Live, it depends on Stage 1 having written the marker before it calls the kickoff. **After the deploy**, on the first tail-minted review: the queued kickoff row's prompt for the minted task contains "is the review task of the `<id>` Periodical, so this run takes no tail". When that review run finishes, its session makes no `/periodicals/*/mint`. **Named rollback**, if a chain is seen: revert PR #2379's merge commit. That is safe, because the PR is prompt text plus an additive response field, with no migration or persisted shape.
- **Inside (spend ceiling, "one Periodical (two sessions)").** The ceiling as approved counts Stage 1 plus Stage 2. Mint-and-stop adds the scoped autopilot orchestrator session that the Mint + Autopilot handoff launches, so one tail costs a mint session plus an orchestrator session plus the review worker sessions. Driving the review inline would have avoided the orchestrator, but not on a `maxTasks` run. **After the deploy**: record the session count of the first live tail on LIN-4349 beside the departure note (`70a5af4c`), so the person sees what one tail actually costs. Same rollback as above.
- **Inside, settled by design (callers passing only `{identifier, title}`).** UI and feedback kickoffs on a review task rely on the policy's marker rule, not the code guard. If a model ignores the rule, it mints at most one more reading. That reading's own handoff goes through the guarded `POST /autopilot/kickoff`, so the chain stops after one step. The Waiting entry in `docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md` stands. This is not a merge condition.
- **Outside (hand mirror).** `docs/autopilot-kickoff.md` is a hand mirror of the kickoff that no test checks. This gap predates this change (survey global, "Better still, not this task's"). Close-out files a follow-up after checking none exists: "docs/autopilot-kickoff.md mirrors lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js by hand with no drift check; add a test or generate the snapshot."

### Verdict
**Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger.**

How the work meets what was asked, sentence by sentence:
- **"Written once, with `landed` ranked under real work."** Met: the leaf, the single Orient rendering, rank 4 and the census.
- **"A scoped run takes one Periodical as it finishes."** Met: the tail in the leaf, the scoped goal block, step 5, the file header and the manual.
- **New import-free leaf rendered in place of both orders.** Met.
- **General order 1–4, and the "can move now" definition.** Met, verbatim.
- **Builder note 2.** Met, including in the tail.
- **The tail: after merge and verify, read, at most one repo-scoped lane, drive its review, stop.** Met. The review is driven through the `autopilot: true` handoff, a change recorded on LIN-4349 as the block allows.
- **Floor before `landed`, then oldest; Recent Headwinds stays with general runs; builder note 3.** Met.
- **Ranks 2 and 4 and the tail go through `POST /periodicals/{id}/mint` with `repo`, keeping the opening `periodicalId` stamp.** Met.
- **Every doc pointer, the Stage B history mark and the session logs left alone.** Met, and the grep is clean.
- **No decision engine.** Met.
- **Acceptance:**
  - the scoped snapshot was updated on purpose, with an after-completion assertion and `never` beside `due`;
  - the anti-duplication test, following the LIN-4374 pattern, covers the lib/routes census and the docs naming the constant;
  - the kickoff ceiling is confirmed absent.
- **Spend ceiling.** Met in structure: one tail per finished scoped task, and P3's one-day landed spacing. The orchestrator-session overhead is a ledger item.
- **"After this lands".** Recorded on LIN-4349, not built here, as asked.

There are no fixes for close-out to make in code. Close-out carries out the post-deploy items above and files the outside follow-up.

## Close-out — LIN-4382

**Merged:** PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2379. The head was `ce92d171215169c2d275d1b5c49970aa0c231e86`. It was merged with `--match-head-commit` as merge commit `a478e5d92ea4535fcf81315e635aed2c1460be28` at 16:08 UTC.
- **Pre-merge CI:** all 7 checks green on `ce92d171` (Unit tests, E2E 1–4/4, Secret scan, CI success; run 42496996734). Merge state was CLEAN. Main had not moved past `393c7686b`, which the head already contained.
- **Post-merge CI:** `Tests` on `a478e5d9` is green (run 42498378651).
